A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A2I research and contain complete, readable main text and appendices. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, six tables, and twelve figures.

before.justification: v4 reports original A2I experiments on text and graph classification, attack-success analyses, and Llama prompting and fine-tuning comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark results, attack-success analyses, and Llama experiments in Section 5 and Appendices B and D.

M1.justification: The A2I architecture, inspection and instruction objectives, and alternating updates in Section 4 and Appendix A.3 are identical. New Appendix E proposes future research directions without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six BeerAdvocate and HotelReview aspect tasks and the BA2Motifs and GOODMotif graph tasks. Appendix E's suggestions about few-shot learning and multimodal models introduce no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each comparison: RNP, InterRAT, NIR, and FR in Tables 1–2; RNP and FR in Table 3; RNP, A2R, CR, and FR in Table 4; and fine-tuned and two-shot Llama in Table 6. The new citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices A and D retain the same splits, sparsity settings, metrics, model configurations, and Llama prompting, fine-tuning, and output-processing procedures.

E4.justification: The random-pattern controls in Figures 3, 9, and 10, instruction-loss and attack-success analyses in Figures 6 and 8, and Llama output case studies in Figures 11–12 are unchanged. Appendix E adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 12252018 for text experiments and averaging over five random seeds for graph experiments. Table 3 retains the same standard-deviation reporting; no statistical or uncertainty procedure changes.

E6.justification: The benchmark entries in Tables 1–4 and 6, attack-success and random-pattern curves, and qualitative Llama findings in Appendix D are identical. Appendix E reports no new outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumption 4.1, Corollaries C.1–C.2, and derivations in Appendix C are unchanged. No equations, formal assumptions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion preserve the same claims about generator-induced spurious correlations in clean datasets, A2I inspection and instruction, and its empirical effectiveness. Appendix E does not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: The existing mechanism explanations, result interpretations, mixed-sentiment qualifications, and limitations of the Llama comparison are unchanged. Appendix E only names possible future research areas, without substantive new interpretation or applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendices A and D retain the same implementation steps, hyperparameters, hardware, LoRA and postprocessing details, and dataset-access instructions. The abstract's code link and its destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix E adds four Tong et al. references: three on few-shot semantic segmentation and FlowCut on efficient vision-language models. This briefly broadens contextual positioning, while the existing references and rationalization-related positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 removes the stray sentence 'The attachments are the new reference letters.' from the Impact Statement, appends the short 'Connection to More Fields' Appendix E, and updates the arXiv version stamp. The existing scientific prose and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The impact-statement edit and added references cause limited text reflow on pages 9–13, and Appendix E fills previously blank space on page 20. All figures and tables retain their content, captions, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: Removing the unrelated sentence modestly improves the Impact Statement's coherence. However, Appendix E adds only broad future-work suggestions and four citations, without developing their connection to A2I. With the scientific argument, evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation unchanged, these limited edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
